title: Adic effectiveness of proper-support flat families
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $\mathcal C(T)$ be the groupoid of pairs $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_BT}$-module, flat over $T$, with support proper over $T$. Here finite presentation means etale locally a cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules; flatness is stalkwise flatness over base local rings on etale charts [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]; proper support means $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X\times_BT$ with $Z\to T$ proper and $N$ finite type quasi-coherent [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Modules and tensor pullback use [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$; composition uses canonical pullback composition isomorphisms. Assume $S$ is locally Noetherian, meaning it has an affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $f$ is separated. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local $S$-algebra, with residue field of finite type over $S$, meaning that $\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m)\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Here local means there is a unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and complete means $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^n$. Restriction is an equivalence from $\mathcal C(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ to the groupoid of compatible systems $x_n\in\mathcal C(\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n))$ with specified pullback isomorphisms for all transitions. In particular each such system is induced by an object over $A$.

proof.text: Write $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^n$ and let $(b_n,M_n)$ be a formal object, including its specified transition isomorphisms. Its base morphisms satisfy $b_n=b_{n+1}|_{\operatorname{Spec}A_n}$. By [lem-sfb-space-complete-local-map-effectivity] there is a unique $b:\operatorname{Spec}A\to B$ restricting to every $b_n$: $A$ is complete, local and Noetherian, as this lemma requires. Thus all the modules live on the thickenings $Y_n$ of the single space $Y=X\times_{B,b}\operatorname{Spec}A$. Use the canonical fibre-product identifications; the given cocycle makes the transition data into a system on these $Y_n$.

source.place: Tag 08W9 (lemma-coherent-existence), first paragraph, reduction to a fixed map to B

proof.text: The morphism $p:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is separated by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], and quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. To verify local finite presentation, take surjective etale scheme charts $V\to B$ and $U\to X\times_BV$. Put $V_A=V\times_B\operatorname{Spec}A$. Then $V_A\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U\times_VV_A\to Y\times_AV_A$ are surjective etale charts. The map $U\to V$ is locally finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test]. On affine pieces its base change is a finitely presented algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1). Thus the base-changed chart map is locally finitely presented, and [lem-sfb-space-local-properties-chart-test] gives the same for $p$. A finite algebra presentation is in particular a finite set of algebra generators, so $p$ is locally of finite type; together with quasi-compactness this is finite type. The identical argument applies to every $Y_n\to\operatorname{Spec}A_n$.

source.place: Tag 08W9 (lemma-coherent-existence), second paragraph, hypotheses on the fixed base change

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-supported-adic-existence] to $Y$, $A$, and $I=\mathfrak m$. Completeness and Noetherianity are hypotheses on $A$, and separatedness and finite type were verified in step 2. Each $M_n$ is finitely presented quasi-coherent and the first has proper support by the formal-object hypotheses. The theorem gives a finitely presented quasi-coherent module $M$ on $Y$, with support proper over $A$, and compatible isomorphisms $M|_{Y_n}\simeq M_n$. It applies to all module homomorphisms, not just isomorphisms. We have not yet asserted that $M$ is flat.

By [lem-sfb-space-adic-flatness-near-closed-fibre], the flat locus $U$ of $M/A$ is open and contains $p^{-1}(\{\mathfrak m\})$: step 2 gives local finite presentation, step 3 gives finite presentation of $M$, and $M|_{Y_n}\simeq M_n$ is flat over $A_n$ for every $n$. Let $C=|Y|\setminus U$. By the proper-support convention [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor], write $M\simeq i_*N$ for a closed $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ with $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper. Outside $|Z|$ this module is zero (restriction of the direct image of a closed immersion there is zero), hence flat. Therefore $C\subseteq|Z|$. Its inverse image in $|Z|$ is closed, with image in the base equal to $p(C)$. Properness includes universal closedness [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], so $p(C)$ is closed. A nonempty closed subset $V(J)$ of the spectrum of a local ring contains its maximal ideal, since every proper ideal $J$ lies in $\mathfrak m$. This contradicts $C\cap p^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\varnothing$. Thus $C$ is empty, $M$ is flat everywhere, and $(b,M)$ algebraizes the given object with every specified transition.

source.place: Tag 08W9 (lemma-coherent-existence), last paragraph, flatness; proper-support globalization made explicit

proof.text: Restriction is well-defined by [lem-sfb-space-module-base-change-flat-proper-support], since $p$ is locally of finite type. For full faithfulness let $(b,M)$ and $(b',M')$ be two objects over $A$. If $b\ne b'$, a formal arrow between their restrictions would imply $b|_{A_n}=b'|_{A_n}$ for every $n$, contradicting injectivity in [lem-sfb-space-complete-local-map-effectivity]; both arrow sets are therefore empty. If $b=b'$, full faithfulness in [lem-sfb-space-supported-adic-existence] lifts each compatible family of isomorphisms $M|_{Y_n}\simeq M'|_{Y_n}$ to a unique module map $h:M\to M'$. Lift their inverses to $k:M'\to M$ by the same theorem. Faithfulness gives $kh=1_M$ and $hk=1_{M'}$, because these equalities hold after every restriction. Hence $h$ is an isomorphism, uniquely lifting the formal arrow. We have proved full faithfulness and essential surjectivity, which give the stated groupoid equivalence.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q57-98debfab5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, the three new nodes and every cited statement in full. Item vs source: Stacks quot.tex 08KB/08W9; the statement is unchanged from base and live, where the item is still unsplit with no reviewed record, so there is no supersession. The five steps follow the 08W9 proof in order. Step 1: 07X8 Case II, i.e. formal-spaces 0AQH, which I checked. Step 2: separatedness, quasi-compactness and local finite presentation by base change, all checked; local finite presentation goes chart-wise through the Mathlib leaf for finitely presented algebras, against the pointwise def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation. Step 3: Grothendieck existence 08BE/08BF with I=m; all its hypotheses hold, and it correctly gives no flatness. Step 4: 08VP plus openness of the flat locus (theorem-openness-flatness); the globalization is written out and correct: the non-flat locus lies in the proper support, its image in Spec A is closed, so if nonempty it contains m, a contradiction. Step 5: full faithfulness, using injectivity on base maps and lifting both an arrow and its inverse. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. New nodes: 0AQH map effectivity (no separatedness on B, correct); 08BE existence with coherent written as finitely presented by lemma-coherent-Noetherian; 08VP, with the source's two typos corrected and reported. Each was tested on small cases, including the k[t], I=(t) example. They are not duplicates of the scheme Grothendieck-existence nodes, of lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-support-inverse-effectivity (0CXB: flat modules, existence only), or of the ring-level 00MK node. None restates a clause of the item, and all are statement-only, unsplit and searched. No SGA citation. The declared tool use of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition is accepted.
